title: Page navigation marks ordinary reads as source scans and disables the Queue quick-link focus target
observed_behavior: Every page change now calls refreshAll with queueRefresh:true. The shared refresh view interprets that option as a real Queue source scan: it disables the Scan Sources button, changes its text to Scanning..., and sets aria-busy. The Queue source inventory quick link then attempts to focus that disabled button and cannot do so. An ordinary read-only page refresh is consequently presented as a source scan even though no scan mutation was submitted.
expected_invariant: Automatic page navigation may enqueue or coalesce read refresh work, but it must not claim a backend source scan is running, disable the scan command, or make a declared quick-link destination unfocusable unless an actual source-scan command owns that state.
root_cause: showPage reuses the queueRefresh option both to request queued automatic refresh scheduling and to signal Queue source-scan busy state. Those are distinct concepts, but refresh.js treats queueRefresh:true as authorization to run setQueueRefreshButtonBusy(true).
failure_scenario: An operator opens Queue, then activates the source inventory tile. Navigation has already started an ordinary GET refresh with queueRefresh:true, so Scan Sources is disabled and relabeled Scanning.... The tile cannot move keyboard focus to the promised control; assistive-technology state falsely reports a backend scan, and the operator cannot start an actual scan until the unrelated refresh settles.
evidence: navigation.js lines 195-211 invokes refreshAll({ automatic: true, queueRefresh: true, page: normalized }) for every page transition
adjacent app/refresh.js lines 9-20 disables and relabels [data-queue-refresh-button] as Scanning... when busy, while lines 150-165 activate that state whenever options.queueRefresh is true
tests/webview/test_webview_browser_home_live_state_smoke.py lines 579-585 requires the Queue source quick link to focus Scan Sources without posting
the exact-current focused browser test deterministically timed out waiting for document.activeElement to become the disabled Scan Sources button
existing_safeguards: the quick link performs no mutation POST
the browser smoke asserts that activating the tile does not post
the button exposes disabled and aria-busy state while the option is active
safeguard_gap: The existing state is internally consistent only for a real scan; it cannot distinguish an ordinary page-read refresh from source-scan lifecycle state, and a disabled HTML button is not a valid focus destination.
tests_present: tests/webview/test_webview_browser_home_live_state_smoke.py contains the exact focus/no-POST regression and currently fails
tests/webview/test_webview_navigation_static.py covers navigation structure but does not reject false queue-scan busy state
tests_missing: a passing browser regression proving ordinary page navigation leaves Scan Sources enabled, correctly labeled, and focusable
a focused refresh-state test distinguishing automatic read queueing from an actual Queue scan command
recommended_remediation: Separate refresh scheduling/coalescing from source-scan busy state. Use a scheduling-only option for showPage, reserve queueRefresh (or a clearly named scanBusy token) for an actual backend source-scan lifecycle, and preserve the Queue quick link's focus contract. Keep the existing no-POST assertion and add explicit enabled, label, aria-busy, and focus checks.
remediation_risk: Low to medium: option renaming touches shared refresh coordination, so verify coalescing and all callers; no media processing or filesystem mutation is involved.
validation_rung: Node syntax checks plus focused navigation/refresh static tests and the Home live-state browser smoke. No representative real-media validation is required.
prior_audit_relationship: Exact path-local finding searches found no prior finding for queueRefresh, false Scanning state, the Queue source-tile focus target, or this navigation regression. Existing W07 findings concern different root causes.
